meta.projection: clip to [0,1], divide by row sum (zero rows guarded); same as fe_surrogate.experiment.renorm

projection_reproduces_stored_renorm_mae._note: rf/xgb/ridge/knn stored renorm npz is literally renorm(raw npz) (delta 0, max pred diff 0). mlp_renorm is a SEPARATELY trained sigmoid model with the same projection, so projecting mlp_sigmoid reproduces only the projection effect, not the trained weights (small but nonzero MAE delta).

ridge_knn_closure_vs_negativity._note: ridge closes the row sum to ~1e-10 (mean closure 1.3e-10..3.7e-10) yet 17-28% of its cells are negative (min about -0.54): negativity, not closure, is the binding violation. knn raw is a convex combination of training targets, so it has NO negative cells and lies in [0,1]; its only residual is a ~1e-9..1e-8 row-sum closure gap. For both, the projection changes MAE only at the 1e-6 level or below relative terms.
